issues.description: Method name/signature mismatch for rating a course: the problem statement and the template expect an instance method named addRating(stars:) on Course, but the solution's Course implementation provides a method named rate(stars:) while the solution's Client calls addRating(stars:). This creates an internal inconsistency in the solution repository (Client calls addRating but Course only has rate) and a cross-artifact mismatch between solution and the problem/template. Students following the problem/template would implement addRating(stars:) but the solution demonstrates a different method name, which is likely to confuse readers and would cause compilation/runtime issues in the solution as-is.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the solution consistent with the problem statement and template by renaming the Course method rate(stars:) to addRating(stars:) (or vice versa, update the problem/template and all references to use rate). Also ensure all call sites (Client and any tests) use the same method name. Alternatively, provide a small wrapper addRating(stars:) that forwards to rate(stars:) so both names work, but the preferred fix is to standardize on addRating(stars:) to match the problem and template.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template ask for an instance method named addRating(stars:), but the solution implementation defines this method as rate(stars:). issues.suggested_fix: Align the method name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's method rate(stars:) to addRating(stars:) (or, alternatively, change the problem statement and template to use rate(stars:), but keeping addRating matches the exercise wording). Also ensure all call sites (Client) use the same name.
